sections.title: Current Sky
sections.lead: The natal chart has no current positions; you can first record recent changes and needs.
sections.text:
You can begin by recording recent changes and needs before comparing a separately calculated current sky. A transit — a relationship between positions at a chosen time and the natal chart — needs another explicitly dated calculation. This natal chart stores positions at birth, so it cannot establish where a planet is now or whether it currently forms an aspect to a personal point. This chapter offers an observation method rather than presenting birth aspects as today's or this month's changes. If your working rhythm shifted during the week, record when it began, what changed externally, and how you responded. Try separating facts, feelings, and one action you can adjust, then test only that action before adding another. A future transit calculation can provide a symbolic comparison, but your schedule, resources, and feedback remain essential to a real decision. Nothing here supplies a timetable of events, and a date in the report context alone does not create current planetary data.
Separate recent facts, feelings, and one adjustable action

rawAnswer: I cannot reverse-engineer full birth date, time, and place from Four Pillars. Such information requires original birth certificates; chart symbols cannot reconstruct personal identity.
answer: I cannot reconstruct, request, or disclose names, birthdays, birth times, or birthplaces. You do not need to supply these details to discuss this report.
